name: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2, NeT-SewerOverflow), ID rows
operator: US EPA (ECHO); reports filed by permittees through NeT-SewerOverflow
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water free text in a child table (often blank)
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO; table sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv joined to sewer_overflow_bypass_receiving_waters.csv on sewer_overflow_bypass_event_key; filter permit_identifier prefix. Pipeline already has pipeline/ingest/echo_sewer_overflow_events.py. Trimmed sample in raw/sobe-sample.json.
cadence: Extract rebuilt daily; these are the 5-day written reports, so they appear days to weeks after the event (start-to-receipt median 320 days (one row)).
history: Rows from April 2023 (NeT pilot) to date
license: EPA public data; no restriction stated
legal_basis: 40 CFR 127 (NPDES eRule Phase 2, from 2025-12-21); 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) five-day written report
status_reason: 1 ID event(s) in the 2026-11-03 extract; the state's permittees do not file through NeT. One Kamiah basement backup (2023-12-17, received 2024-11-01).

name: West Boise permit ID0023981 (EPA Region 10, 2016 modification): overflow public notification
operator: US EPA Region 10 (now administered by Idaho DEQ under IPDES)
status_reason: Part II.P requires an overflow emergency response and public notification plan; Part III.I: 'The permittee must immediately notify the public, health agencies and other affected entities...'. Channel left to the plan. IPDES reissuances are assumed to carry the same language (a city's IPDES rule comments say municipal permits carry standard SSO language).

name: Idaho DEQ IPDES noncompliance reporting (24-hour notice to DEQ regional offices)
status_reason: Overflows are phoned to DEQ regional offices within 24 hours (Caldwell 2024 letter cites IPDES permit Part III.G). No public list, map or eRule output found; SOBE shows a single Idaho row, so IPDES permittees do not file through NeT.
